Group 1 (Case 1):
Here is the student’s answer for this case:
1. Case 1: Myoclonus: uremic encephalopathy
The patient's synchronous, stimulus-sensitive myoclonus with preserved consciousness, markedly elevated BUN/creatinine, low serum sodium, and normal ionized calcium/magnesium converge on uremic encephalopathy. Preserved consciousness argues against seizure; normal calcium/magnesium reduces electrolyte-imbalance myoclonus. Drug-induced myoclonus from bumetanide/dobutamine remains possible, but unavailable medication timing lowers confidence. Missing EEG and dialysis status prevent full certainty, yet the evidence most strongly supports uremic encephalopathy.
